name: webkit-provider
purpose: Sets the language and text direction of every WebKit component below it. It wraps the app once, at the root, with the user's BCP 47 locale: components then read their built-in strings (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) from the locale catalog and format dates, numbers, file sizes, relative times and plurals with `Intl` for that locale. English is built in; Portuguese (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR`) and Spanish (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/es`) are separate entries the app imports and passes through `catalogs`, so an English-only app does not ship them. The catalogs are static imports, so the server and the client render the same strings and hydration never flips after the first render. Digits are Latin unless the tag picks a numbering system (`ar-u-nu-arab`): engines ship different CLDR defaults (Node and Chromium format `ar` with Latin digits, Safari with Arabic-Indic ones), so every `Intl` formatter receives the tag through `intlLocale`, and server and client render the same text. With no provider mounted every component falls back to English. It also carries the reference time of relative times (`now`), so a page that must render the same text on the server and the client, or an example, fixes it once instead of on every cell. The element it renders carries `lang` and `dir`.
useWhen: Once at the root of every app, with the locale the user chose (`pt-BR`, `en`, `es`) and the catalogs of the languages the app offers.
Around one region that must read in another language than the rest of the page (a preview of an email in the customer's language).
To rename a built-in string for the whole app (`messages`), instead of passing the same label prop to every instance.
avoidWhen: Translating your own product copy (titles, descriptions, button labels you pass in) → keep it in your app's own i18n; the provider only covers the strings WebKit ships.
Changing one instance's label → pass the component's label prop (`aria-label`, `confirm-label`); a prop always wins over the catalog.
Only flipping the layout for a right-to-left language → still use the provider with that locale; `dir` follows it.
related: use-locale` — the composable components use to read the active locale, translate a key and format with `Intl`; use it in your own components to match WebKit's formatting.
pagination` — reads its labels and the "Showing x to y of z" line from the catalog.
confirm-dialog` — reads Confirm and Cancel from the catalog when no label is passed.
bestPractices: Mount one `WebkitProvider` at the app root and pass the locale the user chose; do not nest one per page.

Register every language the app offers in `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>`; a `pt-BR` or `es` locale with no registered catalog falls back to English and warns once in development.
Use a full BCP 47 tag (`pt-BR`, not `pt`); a tag with no registered catalog falls back to the same language, then to English.
Override built-in strings through `messages` (partial, deep-merged), not by forking components.
Leave `dir` on `auto`: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu locales turn the subtree right-to-left.

Leave `now` unset in an app: relative times then read the real clock and `Table.CellTime` re-renders every minute. Set it to a fixed moment where the text must not depend on when it renders: an example or a test (`const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 10, 12)`, sample dates counted back from it), or a server render whose markup the browser hydrates. Never compute that moment from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup: the server and the browser read different clocks.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale of everything below the provider; picks the catalog from `catalogs` (English is built in) and the `Intl` formats.

props.name: catalogs
props.doc: Extra catalogs keyed by locale tag, imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`); a locale with no catalog falls back to English.

props.name: messages
props.doc: Partial catalog deep-merged over the built-in one, keyed by component group (`{ pagination: { next: 'Seguinte' } }`).

props.name: dir
props.doc: Text direction of the subtree; `auto` derives it from the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left).

props.name: now
props.doc: Reference time for every relative time below the provider (`Table.CellTime`, `useLocale().formatRelativeTime`); unset reads the real clock, ticking each minute.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The app, or the part of it that shares this locale.

examples.name: Default
CustomMessages
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'

  const messages = {
    pagination: { info: '{start}–{end} de {total} domínios' }
  }
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    locale="pt-BR"
    :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }"
    :messages="messages"
  >
    <PaginationRoot :total="48" />
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>

examples.name: RightToLeft
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider locale="ar">
    <PaginationRoot :total="48" />
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
